text_read: Chapter v 'Eight Steps to Absorption' read in full on the signs (source lines 1-75 summary of the eight steps, 400-780 on Contact, Fixing and the three signs); Chapter vi 'Obstacles to Absorption' read at lines 790-900, 1040-1135, 1490-1520; grep for sign, nimitta, image, light, colour, seen, eyes, visuali.
mode_evidence: Buddhadasa defines both higher signs as mental images: the acquired sign (uggaha-nimitta) 'is visualized, seen by the inner eye. Being a mental image', and the counterpart sign (patibhaga-nimitta) 'is also a mental image'. The test he gives for the acquired sign (corpse example) is that it 'can be seen with the eyes shut at least as clearly as with them open'. For breath the counterpart sign may be 'felt' (cotton, smoke at the contact point) or 'seen vividly' (round object hanging at the nostril, gem, pearl, very large sun or moon), and it may move to chest or navel or 'hang somewhere in front of the meditator'. He attributes its form to the individual's stored memories surfacing from the unconscious. So: a mind's-eye image that becomes vivid and object-like, never said to be in the physical visual field.
onset_evidence: A procedure for producing the sign: count, connect, then narrow attention to the single point where air touches the nostril, visualise that point 'as a sensitive wound against which some object is rubbing', ignore the breath as a whole; this 'results in the formation of a mental image', the acquired sign (a white point or spot at the nose tip). If the counterpart sign does not appear it is because the breath is not felt at the contact point: breathe strongly and start again. Some objects (concepts such as Buddha's virtues) cannot yield an acquired sign at all. No time scale.

conditions.prerequisites: Counting and Connecting (breath followed whole) before Contact; breath progressively finer.
conditions.other: Kasina comparison: blue or red disc about six inches across set in front of the meditator.

stages.label: Preparatory Sign (parikamma-nimitta)
stages.description: The external object: in anapanasati the moving breath itself; in kasina the disc; in asubha the corpse. Counting and Connecting.

stages.label: Acquired Sign (uggaha-nimitta)
stages.description: Mental image 'seen by the inner eye'; in breath practice a white point or spot at the nose tip, formed by attending exclusively to the contact point (Contact, phusana). Changes as the breath grows finer and as personal memories intrude.

stages.label: Counterpart Sign (patibhaga-nimitta)
stages.description: Modified, stabilised form of the acquired sign; felt as cotton or smoke, or seen as a hanging round object, gem, pearl, cotton seed, peg, flowers, garland, spiral of smoke, cobweb, cloud film, lotus, wheel, or a very large sun or moon. Can be shifted at will and is 'nailed' (Fixing, thapana); then absorption.

what_to_do_with_light: Stabilise: once the counterpart sign appears, put the breath aside and attend to the sign directly; if it moves to chest, navel or in front, move the point of Fixing with it; it can be enlarged, reduced, shifted at will and then fixed in the form most suitable for absorption.
obstacles_and_fixes: Breath too fine to discern, so no sign: breathe strongly and start again, or calmly encourage oneself.
Distraction between breath and sign: at the acquired-sign stage attend to the contact point only; at the counterpart stage attend to the sign only.
Do not be disturbed by the unpredictable forms of the sign; delving into them is 'another branch of psychology'.
Tendency to project images (sensual over-sensitivity): check with mindfulness.
cautions: A concept-object such as the Buddha's virtues should not turn into an image; if it does (for the creed-bound) the image is a digression.
interpretation: The signs are mind-made images, conditioned by the breath's fineness and by the individual's stored memories; they matter only as a stable support for absorption.
practice_summary: Begin by counting the breaths, then follow the whole breath without counting. When the mind is steady, drop the breath as a whole and put attention only on the point where the air touches the nostril, picturing it as a sensitive wound being rubbed as air passes. Attend to that point exclusively; a mental image forms there, typically a white point or spot (acquired sign). As the breath grows finer it changes; let it settle into a fixed form (counterpart sign): cotton, smoke, a pearl or gem at the nostril, a cobweb, lotus or wheel, or a large sun or moon. Then attend to the sign directly and let the breath run by itself. If the sign drifts to the chest, navel or in front of you, move your attention with it. Learn to enlarge, shrink and shift it, then fix it in one form until absorption.

key_passages.locator: Ch. v, the three signs, printed pp. 155-156, source lines 494-507
key_passages.anchor: This sign is visualized, seen by the inner eye. Being a mental image
key_passages.paraphrase: Preparatory sign = the breath; acquired sign = a mental image seen by the inner eye, in anapanasati a white point or spot at the nose tip; counterpart sign = also a mental image, a modified form of the acquired sign, shiftable at will.

key_passages.locator: Ch. v, kasina and asubha comparison, printed pp. 156-158, source lines 527-592
key_passages.anchor: so that it can be seen with the eyes shut at least as clearly as with them open
key_passages.paraphrase: Kasina: preparatory work ends when the disc can be seen clearly 'in his mind's eye'; the acquired sign is the internal image, then enlarged or reduced at will and 'nailed' as the counterpart sign. Corpse: the acquired sign is the image seen with eyes shut as clearly as open.

key_passages.locator: Ch. v, anapanasati signs, printed pp. 158-159, source lines 597-613
key_passages.anchor: This point is visualized as a sensitive wound against which some object is rubbing roughly in and out
key_passages.paraphrase: Induction: attend exclusively to the contact point, visualised as a sensitive wound; this produces the acquired sign.

key_passages.locator: Ch. v, printed pp. 159-160, source lines 619-645
key_passages.anchor: another type of person who sees the Counterpart Sign as a very large sun or moon
key_passages.paraphrase: Counterpart sign forms by type of person: felt as cotton or smoke; seen vividly as hanging round object, gem, pearl; peg, flowers, smoke spiral; cobweb, clouds, lotus, wheel; very large sun or moon.

key_passages.locator: Ch. vi, Initial Obstacle, printed pp. 166-167, source lines 873-881
key_passages.anchor: it may move outside and hang somewhere in front of the meditator
key_passages.paraphrase: The counterpart sign can move from the contact point into the chest or navel or outside, hanging in front of the meditator; the point of Fixing follows it.
